I definitely don't think the attacks were a conspiracy. The governments are so inept that it really doesn't surprise me that something like that would happen. Hell, there were numerous terrorist attacks on the buildings before hand.

What is shady? The fact that Saudi Arabia was funding most of it, and where do America invade? Iraq. Because that is where Dick Chenny's company made the most money by taking over operation of oil fields for 'security' purposes, and America was able to control important oil pipe lines.

Jokes on them, China, India, Russia and other major global players are moving into Nuclear energy now, and America will get left behind in the dirt.

In short, yes.

This does not mean that everyone in government was "in" on it. But it does mean that some agents in the US govermnent are at least complicit in the events and in the subsequent coverup and use of deceptive propaganda around the issue.

Who really knows? In the era of revisionist history we are living in, it, and everything else is a matter of opinion subject to be rewritten and revised however it can be most useful. My gut feeling is that yes, our government was a willing participant, but admittedly, I don't have much to back it up: Good information (not slanted, or propaganda-tinged) from shortly before event, event, and the years following is scarce. People have injected so much emotion, and bullshit, into it that it's pretty hands off for a logical extraction of facts anymore. So many different versions of 'the truth' but no way to know for sure what really happened and what was smoke and mirrors sponsored by various political agendas.
